message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to not want to share an Animal Crossing town with my girlfriend. Let me start by understanding the situation better. So, there's this new Animal Crossing game coming out, and each Nintendo Switch console can only have one village. Both my girlfriend and I have our own Switch consoles. She wants us to share one village so we can both use one Switch to play together. But I prefer us both getting the game so we can play online and customize our towns the way we want. I even offered to buy her the game, but she said she wants to feel a sense of "togetherness" in Animal Crossing, which I just don't get. When I insisted on playing on different consoles, even with valid reasons, she got really upset, called me a asshole baby, and told me to grow up. I love the Animal Crossing series, and I want to be able to make my village the way I want. I also want to be able to play with her online. Hmm, so is it right or wrong for me to want to have my own village? On one hand, I understand that she wants to feel connected by sharing a village. But on the other hand, I feel like I should be able to customize my own space and play the game how I want. Maybe I should think about why she feels the need to share a village. Is it because she wants to spend time together, or is it something else? And why do I feel so strongly about having my own village? Is it about personal space or creative control? I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe we can have separate villages but still play together online. That way, she can feel connected, and I can have my own space. But she didn't seem open to that idea when I suggested it. I'm also thinking about how this relates to trust and respect in the relationship. If I'm not willing to compromise, does that mean I'm not respecting her needs? Or is she not respecting mine by insisting on sharing? It's also a bit frustrating that she got so upset. I mean, it's just a game, right? But clearly, it's important to her, and I don't want to hurt her feelings or damage our relationship over something like this. Maybe I should try to understand her perspective better. Why does she feel that sharing a village is important for our togetherness? Is there a way to make both of us happy? I also think about how this might be a bigger issue in our relationship. If we can't agree on something as small as a video game, what does that say about our ability to handle bigger issues? But at the same time, I don't want to give up something that's important to me just to keep the peace. I need to feel like I'm being true to myself. I guess I'm stuck between wanting to please her and wanting to stay true to my own preferences. It's a tough spot to be in. Maybe I should talk to her again and see if we can find a compromise. If she's really insistent on sharing a village, maybe I can try it for a little while and see how it feels. But I'm worried that it might not work out, and then we'll be back to the same argument. Alternatively, maybe I can suggest that we each have our own villages but still play together online. That way, we both have our own spaces, and we can still enjoy the game together. I also wonder if there's a way to make the shared village feel more like our own space together, instead of one person's space. Maybe we can take turns making decisions or collaborate on the design. But I'm not sure if that's what she wants. She seems to want to feel a sense of togetherness, which might mean more than just sharing a village. It might be about spending time together and doing something together that we both enjoy. In that case, maybe the issue isn't just about the village, but about how we spend our time together. If she feels like we're not spending enough time together, maybe she's using the Animal Crossing game as a way to create that connection. If that's the case, then maybe I need to think about how we can spend more time together in ways that we both enjoy, not just through the game. But I still feel strongly about having my own village. I don't want to compromise on that. I guess I need to find a balance where both of our needs are met. It might take some negotiation and compromise, but I think it's worth it to maintain a healthy relationship. Maybe I should also consider whether this is really that big of an issue. Is it worth damaging our relationship over? Probably not. So, I need to find a way to resolve this that works for both of us. I think the key is communication. I need to talk to her about how I feel and listen to her perspective. Only then can we find a solution that works for both of us. Overall, I think it's important to respect each other's preferences and find a middle ground. It might not be perfect, but it's better than being at odds over something like this.
